# Evidence Plane: SBOM, Provenance and Audit Artifacts

This document describes the evidence plane implemented for the project.

The purpose of the evidence plane is to provide traceability for security-relevant development activity. Instead of relying only on manual claims, the CI/CD pipeline generates artifacts that can be reviewed after each pull request or workflow execution.

## Evidence generated by CI

The pipeline generates the following artifacts:

| Artifact | Purpose |
|---|---|
| SBOM | Lists project dependencies and components for supply-chain transparency |
| Go test report | Shows backend test execution results |
| Go test log | Keeps raw backend test output for debugging and audit |
| Go vulnerability report | Records dependency vulnerability checks for the Go backend |
| Frontend audit report | Records dependency audit results for the frontend, where applicable |

## Security relevance

The project processes sensitive medical information and includes multiple services such as the web API, MQTT broker, OCR sandbox and database. Because of this, the development process must provide evidence that security checks were performed.

The evidence plane supports:

- dependency traceability;
- vulnerability analysis;
- test evidence;
- reproducibility of CI/CD checks;
- auditability of pull requests and security decisions.

## SBOM and provenance

The Software Bill of Materials is generated automatically during CI execution. It provides an inventory of the software components used by the project and supports later vulnerability analysis and dependency review.

## Audit artifacts

CI outputs are uploaded as GitHub Actions artifacts. These artifacts can be downloaded from the workflow run page and used as proof that tests and security checks were executed.

## Current scope

This implementation focuses on CI-generated evidence artifacts. Future extensions may include:

- signed provenance attestations;
- immutable external log storage;
- release-attached SBOMs;
- dedicated audit dashboards;
- long-term retention of security evidence.
